result.summary: Replaces the external Boost.Test unit test framework with an in-tree runner and assertion framework implemented in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp}. Assertion macros use expression decomposition to report operands automatically when checks fail, and backward-compatible BOOST_* macro shims are retained so existing tests continue to work without modification. The build system and packaging scripts across CMake, depends, Guix, and vcpkg are updated to drop Boost.Test.
result.problem: Boost.Test imposes external dependency maintenance overhead, requires build-system workarounds in Guix and depends, and suffers from fragmented assertion macros where common checks (like BOOST_CHECK) omit evaluated operand values when tests fail.
evidence: Replacing Boost.Test has been an ongoing objective discussed across RFC #34666 and issue #8670, and motivated by platform-specific runtime issues like #36045 ('test: avoid undersized Boost.Test signal stacks').

PR description details inconsistent developer ergonomics: 'When using boost, there are 3 ways of writing the same thing, each with different outcomes... failures show the expression, but no values for expr1 and expr2.'

enables: Incremental migration of unit tests from legacy BOOST_* macros to native CHECK, REQUIRE, and TEST_CASE macros.

result.scope_notes: Although touching 170 files, over 150 of them are mechanical include changes executed by a scripted-diff replacing Boost headers with the new framework header. The core logic is isolated in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp} (~1,280 lines) and accompanying build configuration files.
result.changed_since_previous: Includes adjustments for expression decomposition operator precedence (wrapping logical and bitwise expressions in test macros), static assertion checks requiring stringification for evaluated types, and a gcc12 warning workaround for CRecipient.
result.card: This pull request replaces Boost.Test across all unit tests with an in-tree test runner and assertion framework in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp}. Boost.Test introduces dependency maintenance costs, requires build-system workarounds in Guix and depends, and features fragmented assertion macros that often omit operand values when tests fail. Replacing Boost.Test has been a long-standing goal tracked in RFC #34666, issue #8670, and motivated by runtime issues like #36045. Although touching 170 files, the diff is predominantly a mechanical scripted-diff of includes, with legacy BOOST_* macros retained as shims to avoid rebasing conflicts for existing pull requests. Boost.Test dependencies are dropped across CMake, depends, Guix, and vcpkg.

risk.why: A flaw in the test framework or expression decomposition could cause failing test assertions to spuriously pass or misreport failures in unit tests.
